title: Positively curved Einstein four-manifolds
main_claim: Every connected closed Einstein 4-manifold with strictly positive sectional curvature is, up to scaling, isometric to round S^4, round RP^4, or Fubini–Study CP^2. The argument runs: (1) a radial upper volume deficit plus the characteristic identities force the two Weyl moments to be equal when both blocks are nonzero; (2) a weighted Hessian inequality, coupled across the two blocks, forces one Weyl block to vanish; (3) a conditional lower volume bound excludes n_+=2, so the gap equality case makes the curvature parallel; (4) a global continuation and orientation-cover argument finishes the classification.

Checked numerically:
- Cubic bound (13) on the actual 12-dimensional Bianchi space: the maximum ratio is 0.61968, equal to (4/5)√(3/5), so the bound is sharp.
- I2 ≤ 2Θr (as a 6×6 matrix inequality), I0 ≤ −Θ²/c, and quartic (19) ≤ −cj, on 300k–400k random spectral and gradient samples with x+y<2; all hold, tight only near v=b=1.
- Moment obstruction lemma: the supremum of J over all feasible measures, by LP, is −0.046 < 0.
- η+ = 0.0819 > 3/40.
- Lower volume bound: 1.3457 > 4/3, and 1.343 with the rational minorants.
